issues.legal_issue: A separate notice to a public officer is not required to sustain relief against the officer when the suit is against the State, notice was given to the State, and the officer is impleaded as the State’s agency.
material_facts: The lower courts found that the plaintiffs held title to the land in the second property item and granted an injunction against interference with their possession.
The plaintiffs gave notice under Section 80 of the Code of Civil Procedure to the State before bringing suit.
The officer was impleaded as the State’s agency of interference with the plaintiffs’ possession.
The State conceded that, in these circumstances, the officer’s objection based on lack of separate notice had no force.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s reversal of the injunction against the officer was set aside, and the injunction granted by the lower courts was sustained against both the State and the officer.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 80 of the Code of Civil Procedure, where the suit is against the State and the public officer is impleaded as the State’s agency, notice to the State suffices in the circumstances presented; the State conceded the point. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: appeal_in_injunction_suit and notice_given_to_state and officer_impleaded_as_state_agency and plaintiffs_established_title_to_property

predicates.appeal_in_injunction_suit: The matter is an appeal arising from a suit seeking an injunction against interference with possession.
predicates.notice_given_to_state: The plaintiffs gave notice to the State before bringing the suit.
predicates.officer_impleaded_as_state_agency: The public officer was made a defendant as the State’s agency of interference with the plaintiffs’ possession.
predicates.plaintiffs_established_title_to_property: The courts found that the plaintiffs held title to the property at issue.

issues.definition: When an appeal in an injunction suit involves notice to the State, an officer impleaded as its agency, and established title to the property, separate notice to the officer is not required to sustain relief against that officer.

issues.legal_issue: An occupier without perfected title to State-owned land may be directed to surrender the land while being allowed to remove plantations the occupier raised there.
material_facts: The courts found that the plaintiffs had possessed the State-owned land since 1946 and had raised trees on it.
The plaintiffs had not perfected title by the time they filed suit in 1961, and the courts found them to be trespassers on that land.
The State required the land for a public purpose.
The plaintiffs’ counsel agreed that the plaintiffs would give up vacant possession after receiving time to remove the trees; the Court directed removal and surrender.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiffs were allowed time to cut and remove the standing trees, were entitled to appropriate those trees, and were directed to deliver vacant possession of the land to the State after removal.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the findings that the State owned the land, the plaintiffs had not perfected title, and the plaintiffs had raised the trees while in possession. It directed surrender while allowing removal of the plaintiffs’ plantations. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this direction.

rule.if: appeal_concerning_possession_of_land and occupiers_lacked_perfected_title and state_owned_the_land and occupiers_planted_trees and occupiers_counsel_accepted_surrender_after_removal

predicates.appeal_concerning_possession_of_land: The matter is an appeal concerning a claim to remain in possession of land.
predicates.occupiers_lacked_perfected_title: The occupiers had not acquired perfected title to the land by the time they brought suit.
predicates.state_owned_the_land: The State was found to be the owner of the land.
predicates.occupiers_planted_trees: The occupiers raised trees on the land while in possession of it.
predicates.occupiers_counsel_accepted_surrender_aft: The occupiers’ counsel agreed that the occupiers would surrender the land after having time to remove the trees.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerning possession involves occupiers without perfected title on State-owned land, trees planted by the occupiers, and their counsel’s acceptance of surrender after removal, the occupiers must remove their plantations and surrender the land.
